structured_output.what_is_happening: A 12-minute-old "merci" token, created directly on PumpSwap without going through the pump.fun bonding curve (the address has no pump suffix and migrated_unix is 0), triggered on heavy volume: $355k in the first hour at about $25k market cap, +140% price. It is one of at least 11 "merci" tokens launched within about 25 minutes. The most likely canonical one (9NPmn...pump) came about 24 minutes earlier and sits near $246k market cap. This coin is a late clone with 100% of its LP unlocked. It shows 38 bundler wallets holding about 31% of top-trader share, and 1,821 unique buyers against only 59 unique sellers, a pattern typical of bot or airdrop-style manufactured activity.

narrative.description: 'merci' is a meme or cult ticker (GeckoTerminal links to a tweet from the X account mercicult). The cluster of clones means a real attention spike exists around the name, but it is centred on the earlier pump.fun token.
narrative.why_spreading: Something drove a launch wave of 'merci' tokens in about 25 minutes (probably a viral post). Clone deployers are farming the ticker search traffic.

token_connection.why_this_token: Only the shared name and ticker, plus a GeckoTerminal link to a mercicult tweet. That link could just as easily be pasted onto clones.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 10 same-name tokens. 9NPmn...pump is the earliest (about 24 minutes before this one), at $246k market cap with $929k 1h volume. HE3sA1 is at $185k and 9UpKD at $241k. This coin ranks near the bottom by market cap.

authenticity.evidence: 1,821 unique buyers against 59 unique sellers within 12 minutes, 38 bundler wallets holding about 31% of top-trader share, and a 21% bot/degen rate. Liquidity ($33k) is larger than market cap ($25k), which fits a self-seeded pool that the creator controls. There is no DexScreener profile and no socials.
authenticity.uncertainty: The buyer count could partly reflect real ticker-search spillover from the viral canonical token. GMGN wallet tags are imperfect.

structural_risks: 100% of the LP is unlocked on a creator-seeded PumpSwap pool, so the creator can pull it at any time
Late clone of a trending ticker, the classic setup for a pull-the-LP rug
38 bundler wallets holding about 31% of top-trader share
Buyer/seller asymmetry that looks like bots
GeckoTerminal top-10 at about 80% including the pool

structured_output.counterargument: Clones of a viral ticker sometimes catch overflow flows and run 2-3x when the canonical token gets too expensive. $25k is a low market cap, and 1,800+ buyers is a lot of breadth. Mint and freeze authority are renounced, top-10 holders excluding the pool are only 16%, and the dev holds almost nothing.

structured_output.thesis: This looks like a late, non-canonical clone of a trending ticker. The LP is unlocked and controlled by the creator, and the buy-side activity looks bundled or bot-driven. The most likely outcome is an LP pull or a bleed-out, not a 2x.
